name: NWPU-RESISC45
description: A large-scale benchmark dataset for remote sensing image scene classification, containing 31,500 images covering 45 scene classes with 700 images in each class. The dataset includes images with spatial resolution varying from about 30 m to 0.2 m per pixel, extracted from Google Earth covering more than 100 countries and regions worldwide.
citeAs: Gong Cheng, Junwei Han, and Xiaoqiang Lu. Remote Sensing Image Scene Classification: Benchmark and State of the Art. Proceedings of the IEEE, 2016.
rai:dataCollection: The dataset was extracted from Google Earth by experts in the field of remote sensing image interpretation. Images were carefully selected under all kinds of weathers, seasons, illumination conditions, imaging conditions, and scales. The 31,500 images cover more than 100 countries and regions all over the world, including developing, transition, and highly developed economies.
rai:dataCollectionRawData: Images were extracted from Google Earth (Google Inc.) that maps the Earth by the superimposition of images obtained from satellite imagery, aerial photography and geographic information system (GIS) onto a 3D globe.
rai:dataManipulationProtocol: Images were manually extracted by experts in the field of remote sensing image interpretation. Each image was cropped to a size of 256×256 pixels in the red green blue (RGB) color space.
rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Images were extracted and cropped to 256×256 pixels. The spatial resolution varies from about 30 m to 0.2 m per pixel for most of the scene classes except for the classes of island, lake, mountain, and snowberg that have lower spatial resolutions.
rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Scene classes were selected by first investigating all scene classes of existing datasets to form 30 widely-used scene categories, then searching keywords on Web of Science and Google Scholar to carefully select 15 additional meaningful scene classes, resulting in a total of 45 scene classes. Images were manually extracted and labeled by experts in the field of remote sensing image interpretation.
rai:annotatorDemographics: Experts in the field of remote sensing image interpretation
rai:dataBiases: The dataset has high within-class diversity and between-class similarity, which makes it challenging. Some scene classes have similar global structure or spatial layout (e.g., church and palace, dense residential and medium residential), leading to potential confusion between classes.
rai:dataLimitations: The spatial resolution varies across scene classes, with some classes (island, lake, mountain, and snowberg) having lower spatial resolutions than others. The dataset is designed to be challenging with high within-class diversity and between-class similarity, which may make it difficult for some classification methods.
rai:dataUseCases: The dataset is designed for remote sensing image scene classification tasks. It can be used for training, testing, and validation of various data-driven algorithms including handcrafted feature-based methods, unsupervised feature learning methods, and deep learning-based methods. The paper evaluates methods using two training-test ratios: 10%-90% (70 training samples and 630 testing samples per class) and 20%-80% (140 training samples and 560 testing samples per class).
